Single Sign\-On (SSO) enables enterprise members to log in to TRAE using the company's unified identity authentication system.

After the enterprise administrator configures SSO login in the TRAE Enterprise Console, members only need to enter their enterprise email addresses to be redirected to the enterprise's identity authentication system to complete the login process.

<span id="50e53a52"></span>
## SSO login process

<img src="data:image/svg+xml;base64," />

The participating parties are described as follows:


|**Role** |**Description** |
|---|---|
|User |An enterprise member who wants to log in to TRAE. |
|TRAE Enterprise Console |The platform for managing enterprise\-level configuration. Enterprise administrators can manage SSO login configuration on this platform. |
|TRAE's account service |TRAE's backend service, responsible for SSO configuration matching, identity authentication, and session management. |
|Enterprise's identity authentication service |Enterprise\-owned identity authentication service (IdP), such as Okta, Azure AD, Google Workspace, and more. |


The process is described as follows:


|**No.**  |**Step** |**Description** |
|---|---|---|
|1 |Initiate SSO login |An enterprise member visits TRAE's login page and selects the "Enterprise SSO Login" option. |
|2 |Enter an enterprise email address |The member enters their enterprise email address, and the system finds the corresponding SSO configuration based on the domain of the email. |
|3 |Redirect to the enterprise's identity authentication page |TRAE redirects the member's browser to the enterprise's IdP page (such as Okta, Azure AD, and more). |
|4 |Complete identity authentication |The member completes identity authentication on the enterprise's IdP page (supports account & password, MFA, and other valid methods). |
|5 |Return to TRAE |After successful authentication, the member's browser automatically redirects back to TRAE. |
|6 |Login completed |TRAE's account service verifies the member's identity information, establishes a login session, and then logs the user into TRAE IDE. |


<span id="a569c1e0"></span>
## Configure SSO login

<span id="448392e3"></span>
### Prerequisites

In the enterprise's IdP, create an OAuth application for TRAE and obtain the following information:


* Client ID (usually the application ID)

* Client secret (usually the application secret)

* Relevant OAuth endpoint URLs, including the authorization endpoint, token endpoint, and user info endpoint


<span id="6a762b62"></span>
### Procedure


1. Log in to the [TRAE Enterprise Console](https://console.enterprise.trae.ai/).

2. Go to **Enterprise Setup** \> **General Settings**.

3. In the **More Sign\-In Options** \> **SSO Login** area, click  **···**  \> **Configure**.

   The SSO sign\-in configuration window appears.

4. In the **Callback Address** section, copy the callback address automatically generated by TRAE for your enterprise.

5. Go to the enterprise's IdP service management center, open the OAuth application you created for TRAE Enterprise, and then set the application's redirect address as the callback address copied in the previous step.

6. Return to the SSO login configuration window, then click the **Next** button.

   You will enter the OAuth parameter configuration panel.

   <span>![图片](https://p9-arcosite.byteimg.com/obj/tos-cn-i-goo7wpa0wc/408e110fdf2e4f31a697645f53fb934f) </span>

7. Configure the following OAuth parameters:

   
   |**Parameter** |**Required** |**Description** |
   |---|---|---|
   |Client ID |Yes |The unique identifier of the OAuth application you created for TRAE in the IdP. |
   |Client Secret |Yes |The secret of the OAuth application you created. TRAE uses this secret to exchange for an access token from the IdP. |
   |OAuth URL |Yes |The authorization endpoint of the IdP. Members will be redirected to this page to complete authentication. |
   |Token URL |Yes |The token endpoint of the IdP. TRAE's backend uses this endpoint to exchange the authorization code for an access token. |
   |UserInfo URL |Yes |The user information endpoint of the IdP. TRAE calls this interface to obtain the user's identity information. |
   |Scope |No |The scope of the request, which defines the user information that TRAE can access. Multiple values are separated by English commas. |
   

   <div data-tips="true" data-tips-type="warning" data-tips-is-title="true" data-wrapper-indent="1">Caution   </div>
   

   <div data-tips="true" data-tips-type="warning" data-wrapper-indent="1">The client secret is a highly sensitive credential. Do not expose it to any client\-side code, logs, or version control systems. TRAE uses this secret only between the backend server and the IdP, and will not expose it to the frontend or users.   </div>
   

   For more information about the above parameters, refer to the "SSO configuration details" section.

8. After configuring all required parameters, you can:

   * Click the **Save And Test** button. The system will save the configuration and initiate a real SSO login process to verify your configuration.

   Or

   * Click the **Save Only** button to save the configuration directly.

9. Toggle the **SSO Login** switch on.


<span id="a7ed4665"></span>
## SSO configuration details

<span id="f8290a20"></span>
### Callback address

The OAuth callback address for TRAE is automatically generated by the system and displayed in the first step of the SSO login configuration pop\-up window. Before integrating SSO login, this address must be accurately set as the redirect URL or allowed callback URL of the OAuth application in the IdP.

Note that:


* The callback address must be an exact match (case, path, and trailing slash must all be consistent). The IdP will strictly validate the redirect URL.

* The deployment address for TRAE varies by enterprise. Use the actual address displayed in the pop\-up as the reference.

* If the enterprise has configured a custom domain name for TRAE, the callback address will use the custom domain name.


<span id="fe1669b6"></span>
### "Scope" parameter

The `Scope` parameter is used to declare to the IdP the scope of user information permissions that TRAE needs to obtain. When TRAE uses an access token to call the `UserInfo` interface, the IdP determines which user properties to return based on the authorized permission scope.

In the SSO login configuration form of TRAE, multiple values for the `Scope` parameter are separated by commas, for example:

```Plain Text
openid,profile,email
```


It is recommended to include at least the following permissions to ensure that TRAE can obtain the necessary user information:


|**Value** |**Description** |
|---|---|
|`openid` |Basic OIDC permission, which allows TRAE to obtain the user's unique identifier (`sub`). |
|`profile` |Allows TRAE to obtain the user's name (`name`), avatar, and other basic information. |
|`email` |Allows TRAE to obtain the user's email address (`email`).<br><br>***Caution***: If this permission is not included, some IdP `UserInfo` endpoints will not return the `email` field, resulting in login failure. |


<div data-tips="true" data-tips-type="default" data-tips-is-title="true">Note</div>


<div data-tips="true" data-tips-type="default">Different IdPs may use different names for the value of <code>Scope</code>. If using a non\-OIDC standard IdP (such as an in\-house authentication system), refer to the documentation of that IdP to obtain the correct value.</div>


<span id="1ae57b77"></span>
### "state" parameter

`state` is an anti\-CSRF security parameter in the OAuth 2.0 process, automatically generated by the TRAE server each time an authorization request is initiated. Enterprises do not need to configure it manually.

The IdP must return the received `state` to TRAE by appending it to the callback address without any modification. If `state` is modified or discarded, TRAE will reject the callback request and report an error.

To address behavioral differences among different IdPs, TRAE has built in the following compatibility mechanisms:


* Automatically handles URL encoding (for example, converting `%3D` to `=`).

* Supports both URL\-safe Base64 and standard Base64, with automatic fallback.

* Automatically restores spaces as `+`, and is also compatible with some IdPs that decode `+` as spaces.


<span id="8be5ba18"></span>
### Token exchange authentication methods

When exchanging an authorization code for an access token (calling the Token URL), TRAE uses the OAuth 2.0 Auto\-Detect mode and will automatically detect the authentication method supported by the IdP:


* **Via the header**: Passes `client_id` and `client_secret` through the `Authorization: Basic` request header.

* **Via the body**: Places `client_id` and `client_secret` as parameters in the request body.


TRAE supports both methods; the IdP only needs to support one of them.

<span id="8b8ae7c3"></span>
### UserInfo interface specifications

After obtaining the access token, TRAE will call the configured UserInfo URL to obtain the user's identity information.

<span id="d63bf8f5"></span>
#### Invocation methods

TRAE primarily uses the bearer token in an HTTP request to call the `UserInfo` interface:

```Plain Text
GET {UserInfo URL}
Authorization: Bearer {access_token}
```


If the interface returns a non\-200 status code, TRAE will automatically fall back to the method of querying parameters and retry:

```Plain Text
GET {UserInfo URL}?access_token={access_token}
```


<div data-tips="true" data-tips-type="default" data-tips-is-title="true">Note</div>


<div data-tips="true" data-tips-type="default">TRAE retries up to three times. Both invocation methods will be attempted. It is recommended to ensure at least one method is available.</div>


<span id="a7f021e1"></span>
#### Response field requirements

The `UserInfo` interface must return data in JSON format. TRAE will extract the following fields:


|**Field** |**Type** |**Required** |**Description** |
|---|---|---|---|
|`email` |string |Yes |The user's email address, used for matching with their TRAE account. If missing, login will fail. |
|`sub` |string / number |No (recommended to provide) |The user's unique identifier in the IdP, used for account linking. |
|`name` |string |Yes |The user's display name. If missing, login will fail. |
|`avatar` |string (URL) |No |The user's avatar address. If missing, the user's current avatar in TRAE will be retained. |


**Field extraction order:** 

TRAE first extracts the fields listed in the table above from the root level of the response; if not found, it automatically falls back to look under the `data` field. No additional field mapping configuration is required for enterprises. Both response formats can be correctly parsed:


* Response root level (standard format): `{ "email": " user@example.com", "name": "John" }`

* `data` field (nested format): `{ "data": { "email": " user@example.com", "name": "John" } }`


**Email matching rules:** 

TRAE compares the `email` field returned by the IdP with the email entered by the member on the login page. The two must be identical (case\-insensitive), otherwise the login will be rejected and an "email not match" error will be returned. Enterprises must ensure that members use their enterprise emails registered in TRAE to initiate SSO login.

<span id="c2862b97"></span>
## IdP integration examples

<span id="7523243a"></span>
### Feishu Open Platform

Enterprises can create a custom application on Feishu Open Platform and then directly reuse Feishu's identity system to integrate with TRAE SSO. This is the mainstream method for integrating Feishu with TRAE SSO and is suitable for enterprises that have not yet deployed an independent SSO gateway.


|**Parameter** |**Reference Value** |
|---|---|
|OAuth URL |`https://accounts.feishu.cn/open-apis/authen/v1/authorize` |
|Token URL |`https://open.feishu.cn/open-apis/authen/v2/oauth/token` |
|UserInfo URL |`https://open.feishu.cn/open-apis/authen/v1/user_info` |
|Scope |`contact:user.email:readonly,contact:user.employee_id:readonly` |


**Prerequisites:** 


* Create a custom enterprise application on Feishu Open Platform (open.larkoffice.com).

* In the application's **Development Configuration** \> **Security Settings** section, add TRAE's callback address as the application's redirect URL.

   If you have already created a dedicated domain name for your enterprise, it is recommended to add both the callback address for TRAE Enterprise's public domain (`https://console.enterprise.trae.cn/oauth/callback`) and the callback address for your enterprise's dedicated domain (`https://vpcxxxxxxx.trae.volces.com/oauth/callback`) to avoid SSO login failures caused by subsequent changes to domain access policies.

* In the application's **Development Configuration** \> **Permissions & Scopes** section, enable the following permissions:

   * `contact:user.email:readonly`: Used to obtain the email address

   * `contact:user.employee_id:readonly`: Used to obtain the user ID

* Publish the application and set its visibility scope by adding members who need to log in using TRAE SSO.


<div data-tips="true" data-tips-type="default" data-tips-is-title="true">Note</div>


<div data-tips="true" data-tips-type="default">The <code>UserInfo</code> endpoint of Feishu wraps user information under the <code>data</code> field (such as <code>data.email</code>, <code>data.name</code>). TRAE has built\-in automatic compatibility for this structure, so no additional field mapping configuration is required. The user's email corresponds to <code>data.email</code> (personal email), and the user's unique identifier corresponds to <code>data.open_id</code>.</div>


<span id="ae5ab716"></span>
### Feishu AnyCross

Enterprises can build a unified SSO gateway (aggregating multiple IdPs) on Feishu AnyCross, and then allow TRAE to reuse this unified access point.


|**Parameter** |**Reference Value** |
|---|---|
|OAuth URL |`https://anycross.feishu.cn/sso/{app_identifier}/oauth2/auth` |
|Token URL |`https://anycross.feishu.cn/sso/{app_identifier}/oauth2/token` |
|UserInfo URL |`https://anycross.feishu.cn/sso/{app_identifier}/oauth2/userinfo` |
|Scope |`profile,email` |


**Prerequisites:** 

Refer to [this article](https://anycross.larkoffice.com/documentation/sso/protocol/OAuth) to create a custom SSO application on Feishu AnyCross (anycross.feishu.cn) and enable the OAuth 2.0 protocol. Parameter configuration requirements are as follows:


* Set TRAE's callback address as the application's login callback address.

   If you have already created a dedicated domain for your enterprise, it is recommended to add both the callback address for TRAE Enterprise's public domain (`https://console.enterprise.trae.cn/oauth/callback`) and the callback address for your enterprise's dedicated domain (`https://vpcxxxxxxx.trae.volces.com/oauth/callback`) to prevent SSO login failures caused by subsequent changes to domain access policies.

* Set the authorization mode to `authorization_code`, add `Email` and `profile` as the scope, and set the response type to `code`.

* In the URL, `{app_identifier}` is the unique identifier for a self\-built application on Feishu AnyCross; replace it with the actual value.


<div data-tips="true" data-tips-type="default" data-tips-is-title="true">Note</div>


<div data-tips="true" data-tips-type="default">The UserInfo endpoint of Feishu AnyCross follows the standard OIDC format, with the <code>email</code> and <code>name</code> fields located at the root level of the response. TRAE can parse them directly, with no additional configuration required.</div>


<span id="fRwfxngn"></span>
## Force members to use SSO login 

After setup SSO login for your enterprise, you can force all members to login in to TRAE Enterprise using SSO login only. 


1. Log in to the [TRAE Enterprise Console](https://console.enterprise.trae.ai/). 

2. Go to **Enterprise Setup** \> **General Settings**. 

3. In the **More Sign\-In Options** area, toggle the **Force SSO Login** switch on.
